h1: The 6 Best Easy-to-Use Printers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six easy-to-use home printers compared on setup flow, on-screen guidance, document feeders and ink access.
summary: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the easiest printer for first-time buyers, with a simple wireless setup, a labeled cartridge door and a 3-month Instant Ink trial. The Canon TS6520 adds an OLED display for error messages. The TR4720 brings a document feeder, the TS6420 has labeled buttons, and the TS4320 and TS3720 suit routine and light use.
intro: Printers earn their reputation for being difficult in two moments: the first connection and the first jam. A model that joins your Wi-Fi in a few taps but answers a stuck sheet with a blinking amber light has only solved half the problem. Ease of use, then, is two separate qualities, a good setup flow and good help when something fails, and the best printers cover both.

We judged six home printers on those terms, along with how simply they handle everyday jobs such as copying a form or scanning a receipt. Eight were considered and six ranked from spec sheets, and we did not time any setup ourselves. The Canon line dominates the list for a reason: it offers the widest range of display, button and feeder choices at the price of a modest inkjet.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The simplest start for a first-time printer buyer.
products.description:
HP's DeskJet 4355 earns first place by smoothing the two moments that usually frustrate beginners. A short wireless setup connects it to your network, and a plainly labeled cartridge door takes the guesswork out of changing ink. It prints, scans and copies in color, comes with a 3-month Instant Ink trial and sits in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks above the Canon TS6520 because the setup is described more simply, though it lacks the OLED display that makes error messages readable. A compact body keeps it unintimidating on a shelf.

Buy it for first-time buyers and non-technical households. The caveat is what the small size leaves out: there is no document feeder, so every scan means lifting the lid, and no color display, so you rely on lights when something fails. Heavy scanners should look at the TR4720.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen spells out what is wrong.
products.description:
The Canon TS6520 puts words on the screen. A 1.42-inch OLED display shows status messages in plain language, so a paper jam or low ink reads as a sentence rather than a code. It also prints duplex, includes a built-in copier and scanner, and has an intuitive control panel, in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks second because the display makes troubleshooting less of a guess, but its setup flow is not described as simply as HP's. Where the DeskJet wins on day one, the Canon wins on day thirty, when something breaks.

Buy it if you dread error lights. The caveat is size: the screen is small, so long messages need scrolling, and there is no document feeder, which limits multipage scans. Skip it if you would never look at a display anyway and want the simplest hardware.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want help when something fails.
products.skipIf: You never look at the display.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A document feeder takes the pain out of scanning.
products.description:
The TR4720 is the one that makes scanning painless. It has an automatic document feeder that pulls pages in one at a time, which scanning-heavy homes feel immediately, plus mobile printing, wireless connectivity and a legacy fax, in the $50 to $100 band. Feeding a ten-page form is a single step instead of ten lid lifts.

It ranks third because the feeder simplifies multipage work that none of the higher picks offer, while its day-to-day controls are less guided, with no OLED display. You choose capability over hand-holding.

Buy it for households that scan bills, forms and school paperwork often. The caveat is the fax: it is a legacy feature most people will ignore, and it adds buttons and menus that make the printer look more complicated than it is. If you only print, the TS3720 is simpler.

products.name: Canon TS6420 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Clear button labels and a simple wireless setup flow.
products.description:
The TS6420 is the choice for people who trust buttons over menus. It prints, scans and copies in color, has a simple wireless setup, and a button layout where every key is clearly labeled. Real keys are quicker for a one-touch copy than scrolling a touch menu.

It ranks fourth because it costs a band more than the cheaper Canons, in the $100 to $200 range, without adding a feeder or a display. For the same money you could take a model with more help.

Buy it if you prefer physical controls to touch screens. The caveat is ink: it is cartridge-based, so running costs add up if you print a lot, and the higher price asks you to value the buttons enough to pay for them.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact single-tray printer with app support.
products.description:
The TS4320 keeps things simple: a compact single-tray design with duplex printing and app printing from a phone. A built-in copier and scanner and a 1-year limited warranty come at $50 to $100. One paper tray means one place to load, and a phone app handles the printing for people who never touch a computer.

It ranks fifth because it has none of the guidance extras of the TS6520. It keeps the same duplex and app basics but gives you no display help when a jam occurs, and no feeder.

It suits people who print the same few things each week. The caveat is on-device support, so when something fails you rely on blinking lights and the manual. Choose the TS6520 instead if error messages are a worry, or the TR4720 if you scan.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Stripped down to the basics, with no feeder or fax.
products.description:
Canon's TS3720 is the plain one: a small, inexpensive color printer that scans and copies over wireless, with no document feeder and no fax. It costs $50 to $100. With so few controls, there is little to misunderstand, which is the whole appeal for a nervous user.

It ranks last because it offers the fewest features, yet that is the point for people who want the fewest buttons. Next to the TR4720, it drops the feeder and the mobile printing mention, and next to the TS6520, it drops the display.

It suits light users, older relatives and a printer that sits mostly idle. The caveat is multipage scanning, which is slow without a feeder. Heavy scanning is better done on the TR4720, and anyone who prints a lot should consider a model with more guidance.

whatMatters.detail: Setup is connecting the printer to your Wi-Fi and phone, and a guided flow saves the worst frustration. Look for a described simple wireless setup, as on the HP DeskJet 4355, and have your Wi-Fi password ready. Make sure your phone is on the same network, or the printer will not appear, and expect to enter the password once.

A display explains errors in words instead of blinking lights, which matters most during a paper jam. A 1.42-inch OLED, as on the Canon TS6520, is small but clear. Check whether the listing names a display at all, because many cheaper models rely on indicator lights and a manual, and a light alone rarely says which door is open.

Labeled physical buttons are faster for simple copy jobs than menus, and fewer buttons means less to learn. Look at the product photos for the control panel, and decide whether you prefer keys or a screen. A cluttered panel with legacy fax keys can make a simple printer look hard, even if the daily tasks are easy.

An auto document feeder pulls pages in one at a time for scanning and copying. Without one, you place each page on the glass. If you scan stacks of paper, the feeder is the real ease-of-use feature, and the TR4720 is the only model here that lists one, so it stands apart for paperwork.

A clearly labeled cartridge door makes ink changes less intimidating, and it reduces mistakes like forcing the wrong slot. It is a small detail that matters for first-time buyers. Look for it in the feature bullets, as with the HP DeskJet 4355, and check how ink is replaced, including whether cartridges are cheap and easy to find.

faq.q: Do these need a computer to set up?
faq.a: Most can be set up from a phone app over Wi-Fi, so no computer is required. The HP DeskJet 4355 describes a simple wireless setup flow, which is the easiest start among these for someone who has never set up a printer.
Pairing over the wrong Wi-Fi network. Make sure your phone is on the same network as the printer, and keep the router password nearby before you start the setup, so you do not stall halfway.

faq.q: Is the TR4720 worth it over the TS3720?
faq.a: Yes, if you scan. The TR4720 adds an automatic document feeder, which turns a multipage scan into one step. If you only print and copy, the TS3720 costs the same and has fewer buttons to confuse a newcomer.
Open the labeled access door and follow the prompts. The HP DeskJet 4355 labels the door clearly, and the Canon TS6520 can show a message on its OLED display if a cartridge is wrong or empty.

faq.q: How do I keep ink from drying?
faq.a: Print a page every week or two. Idle inkjets can dry out, so a short routine job keeps the nozzles moving, and any of these printers benefits from regular use. Do not leave one switched off for months.

faq.q: Can I print from a phone?
faq.a: The TR4720 and TS4320 list mobile printing support, and the HP DeskJet 4355 uses a phone for setup. Check the app is available for your phone before buying, and confirm your phone's software is recent enough.

finalTake: Buy the HP DeskJet 4355 if you want the least friction on day one, or the Canon TS6520 if you want plain-language error messages. Choose the TR4720 when scanning stacks of paper is the real job. The TS6420, TS4320 and TS3720 are narrower fits, each for a specific habit or user.
